notes: All facts checked on 2026-10-27 unless a source date is given. Prices are USD list prices as shown by the cited source on that date.
Vectric's own purchase pages load prices client-side and returned no figures; Vectric USD prices are from authorized resellers / Sienci's own store and are marked accordingly.
Nothing here describes CarvCAM pricing. CarvCAM claims in FAQ answers are limited to the product description supplied by the CarvCAM team.

competitors.name: Easel (Basic / Starter / Pro)
competitors.type: Combo: browser-based CAD + CAM + machine control (sender)
competitors.launched: unverified (commonly cited ~2014; not confirmed on a primary source)

pricing.notes: Full design toolset, but only ONE carve or G-code export per week. No V-carving, no 3D carving, one machine profile.
20 carves or G-code exports per week; adds raster carving, ramping plunges, center work zero. Still no V-carving.

Unlimited carves/exports, V-carving, V-carve inlays, 3D carving, 300+ fonts, 10M+ design library, custom bit/material toolbox, large-material tiling, multiple machine profiles, resume carve. Auto-renews.

competitors.platforms: Browser (any OS with a modern browser; Web Serial 'Quick Connect' requires Chrome/Chromium) plus the Easel Driver for USB machine connection
competitors.offline: No. Cloud/browser app; Sienci notes Easel requires an internet connection to work.
competitors.runs_machine: Yes for GRBL and FluidNC machines over USB. For grblHAL (Sienci SuperLongBoard/SLB-EXT) there is an opt-in beta announced October 2026: USB only, no Ethernet/Wi-Fi. Before the beta, SLB users had to export G-code and run it in gSender.
competitors.sienci_support: Easel has a Sienci Labs partner page listing AltMill MK2 4x4 (SLB-EXT), LongMill MK3 (SLB-LITE), LongMill original and LongMill MK2.5. Sienci's post-processor table says 'No selection required' for Easel. grblHAL live carving is beta-only and USB-only.
features: 2D design tools, text, basic shapes, SVG/DXF/G-code import and export
Image trace (image-to-vector)
Built-in bit and material libraries with recommended cut settings; Community Cut Settings
Automated toolpath generation, two-stage carving with feedrate override
Detailed 3D preview / simulation
Raster carving and ramping plunges (Starter and Pro)
V-carving, V-carve inlays, 3D carving, textured pockets, nesting, large-material tiling (Pro only)
Machine setup wizard with wiring test, homing, spindle test, Z-probe (also on grblHAL beta)
Digital readout (DRO), resume carve (Pro), machine parking (Pro)

limits.text: Free Basic plan is limited to one carve or G-code export per week; Starter is limited to 20 per week.
V-carving, V-carve inlays and 3D carving require Easel Pro ($24/mo or $216/yr).
grblHAL support (needed for Sienci SLB/SLB-EXT) is an opt-in beta; Ethernet and Wi-Fi connections do not work, only USB.
For grblHAL controllers outside the beta, Easel exports G-code to run in the machine's own software.
Requires an internet connection; Sienci suggests designing on one computer and running the machine from another if offline.

pain_points.text: New LongMill MK2.5 owner could connect in gSender but Easel Pro could not see the SLB; forum reply: Easel doesn't support grblHAL firmware (pre-beta).
'I just purchased a Sienci Labs Longmill with their SLB controller and come to find out that Easel is incompatable with grblHal.'
Users who only do 2D work dropped Pro after price increases and asked for a cheaper 'pro lite' tier; subscription poor value for occasional users.
Sienci's own 2026 software review: V-bits, ramping, STL import and clip art need Pro; no internet means you can't create new files.
Onefinity forum thread on the Easel price hike: users weighing whether to pay or 'jump ship' to Carbide Create, Carveco or VCarve.

stronger: Fastest first-cut experience; nothing to install, runs in any browser.
Huge tutorial base, project gallery, and 10M+ design library on Pro.
Works across many GRBL machine brands, not tied to one vendor.
Now has a guided setup (wiring test, homing, probe) similar in spirit to CarvCAM's, and is actively adding grblHAL support.
Cloud storage means projects follow you between computers.
Mature product with years of user feedback; Pro adds 3D carving and inlays.

faq.q: Is Easel free?
faq.a: Easel Basic is free but limited to one carve or G-code export per week, and V-carving is not included. Starter ($8/mo) allows 20 per week; Pro ($24/mo, $216/yr) is unlimited.

faq.q: Does Easel work with the LongMill or AltMill?
faq.a: Easel lists Sienci machines on its partner page. Machines with the grblHAL SuperLongBoard can carve live only through an opt-in beta (October 2026) over USB; otherwise you export G-code and run it in gSender.

faq.q: Can I use Easel offline?
faq.a: No. Easel is a browser app that needs an internet connection. CarvCAM is a Windows desktop app that works offline.

faq.q: Does free Easel do V-carving?
faq.a: No. V-carving, V-carve inlays and 3D carving are Easel Pro features.

faq.q: Can Easel connect over Ethernet to the SLB?
faq.a: Not currently. Easel's grblHAL beta page says Ethernet and Wi-Fi do not work yet; USB only. CarvCAM connects over USB or Ethernet.

faq.q: Does Easel use Sienci's feeds and speeds?
faq.a: Easel uses its own bit/material libraries and community cut settings. CarvCAM's defaults come from Sienci's published speed tables for the specific machine, router/spindle and bit.

sources.title: Easel Plans/Pricing (Easel Support Center, updated Aug 14 2026)
Sienci forum: Easel connecting to SLB
Sienci Labs 2026 CNC Design Software Review (YouTube)

competitors.name: gSender
competitors.type: Sender / machine control only (no CAD, no CAM). Includes surfacing g-code generator.
competitors.launched: Public release May 2021, after ~5 months of alpha/closed beta with 300+ testers; built on CNCjs.

pricing.notes: Open source, GNU GPLv3. gSender Edge is a free test build.

competitors.platforms: Windows, Intel Mac, Apple Silicon Mac, Raspberry Pi, Intel Linux; older builds for legacy OSes (Chromebook instructions in docs)
competitors.offline: Yes (desktop app; internet only needed to download/update)
competitors.runs_machine: Yes, this is its job. Supports grbl and grblHAL, USB or Ethernet, wireless control from a second device via browser.
competitors.sienci_support: First-party: Sienci's own sender, works out-of-the-box on LongMill and AltMill with pre-built machine profiles; Sienci recommends it as the go-to interface.
features: Connect over USB or Ethernet; grbl and grblHAL
Jogging, DRO, zeroing, touch-plate probing with continuity detection
3D toolpath visualization and file insight (feed range, tools used, estimated time, dimensions)
Feed/spindle overrides, start-from-line, outline, pause/stop
Tool change handling on M6 (pause, ignore, or run code blocks)
Surfacing tool, squaring/calibration wizard, motor movement tuning
Firmware tool for EEPROM settings and flashing
Macros, keyboard shortcuts, joystick/gamepad support, lightweight mode
Pre-built profiles for LongMill, AltMill, Shapeoko, X-Carve, OpenBuilds, and many more

limits.text: No design or toolpath creation: Sienci's toolchain docs pair gSender with a separate CAM program (e.g., Carbide Create, Vectric, Fusion).
Provided 'as is'; Sienci docs advise holding off updates before important carves and exporting preferences first.
Users must pick the correct firmware (grbl vs grblHAL) at connect; mis-selection caused erratic behaviour, prompting Sienci to change defaults in 1.4.4.

pain_points.text: User reports jobs stopping midway on large Fusion mesh files; turned out to be USB/RF noise, fixed by rerouting the cable.
LongMill MK2.5 owner on Ethernet: gSender 1.6.4 stopped with 'Alarm 10: EStop asserted' and did not record the last line run.
SLB owner: harder and harder to connect at startup; homing button missing until reconnecting several times.
GitHub issue: job stops mid-carve; start-from-line ran at ~1 in/min due to an inch/mm bug, fixed in 1.5.x.
Beginner confusion about the multi-program toolchain: 'have no clue how to get the file to the Longmill.'

stronger: Free and open source, made by the machine maker itself, so it tracks SLB firmware changes closely.
Cross-platform today (Windows, Mac, Linux, Raspberry Pi) while CarvCAM's Mac/Linux builds are still in development.
Deep machine utilities: firmware/EEPROM editor, squaring calibration, motor tuning, surfacing generator, macros, joystick support.
Works with any CAM program you already know; pairs with VCarve, Fusion, Carveco, etc.
Wireless control from a second device through a browser.
Large existing user base and Sienci support documentation.

faq.q: Is gSender free?
faq.a: Yes. gSender is free, open source (GPLv3) software from Sienci Labs.

faq.q: Can gSender design or create toolpaths?
faq.a: No. gSender runs G-code you make elsewhere (it can generate surfacing code). You still need CAD/CAM software. CarvCAM combines design, toolpaths and machine control in one app.

faq.q: Do I have to stop using gSender if I use CarvCAM?
faq.a: No. CarvCAM can run the machine itself, but gSender remains a free option for running G-code from any CAM program, and for firmware utilities.

faq.q: Does gSender work over Ethernet?
faq.a: Yes, gSender connects over USB or Ethernet to grbl and grblHAL controllers including the SuperLongBoard.

faq.q: What platforms does gSender support?
faq.a: Windows, Mac (Intel and Apple Silicon), Linux and Raspberry Pi.

faq.q: Which CAM does Sienci pair with gSender?
faq.a: Sienci's docs show Carbide Create + gSender as an example toolchain, and its product pages say most customers use Vectric VCarve Pro or Carveco with gSender.

competitors.name: Carbide Create (Core / Pro)
competitors.type: CAD + CAM (no machine control; Carbide Motion is the separate sender, Carbide 3D machines only)

pricing.notes: Included with Shapeoko/Nomad. Designed for Carbide 3D machines; saving standard G-code for any CNC machine is a Pro-only feature.
Deactivates at end of term.
One year of updates included; additional updates $120/year.
Fully functional, generates G-code.

competitors.offline: Yes, runs locally; no internet required
competitors.account_required: No account needed for Core use per vendor page (Pro needs license activation; unverified whether activation needs internet)
competitors.runs_machine: No. Carbide Motion (sender) only works with Carbide 3D machines, so LongMill/AltMill owners need Pro to export G-code and then run it in gSender or another sender.
competitors.sienci_support: Sienci's post-processor table lists 'grbl' for Carbide Create. Sienci's docs note that V7+ removed free G-code export, requiring a C2D extraction workaround (now limited to Carbide machine owners) or an older V6 build.
features: 2D design: shapes, Bezier splines, text on arc, booleans, offsets, alignment
Automatic image-to-vector tracing; SVG/DXF import; Design Elements library
Pockets, contours, V-carving, V-carve inlay mode, engraving
Tool library with speeds and feeds; 3D simulation
Pro: 3D modelling (components, textures, heightmaps, STL import), 3D rough/finish, rest machining, ramping, toolpath tiling, advanced engraving, standard G-code output

limits.text: Carbide Create Core is designed for Carbide 3D machines; using it with another CNC machine requires a Pro license.
G-code export is offered only in Create Pro.
Since V7, G-code is stored encrypted inside the .c2d file; the web extraction tool is limited to owners of Carbide 3D machines (since June 30 2023).
Toolpath tiling (to cut larger than the work area) is Pro-only.

pain_points.text: 'If you want to use a non carbide machine you have to pay for pro in order to export G-code now.'
User upset that 'Save as Gcode' was greyed out as Pro-only after updating to V7.
Onefinity owners lost the free C2D-to-G-code web extraction in mid-2023; workaround is downgrading to V6.
Sienci 2026 review: without Pro you can't save real G-code and are 'basically stuck in their ecosystem'.
Older LongMill user opinion: 'poor user interface and limited free functionality.'

stronger: Mature, polished 2D/2.5D design tools with booleans, splines, inlay mode and a large design-element library.
Mac support today.
Pro adds 3D modelling, heightmaps, STL import and 3D roughing/finishing at a low price ($120/yr).
Perpetual license option ($360) for subscription-averse users.
Large tutorial library (My Carbide 3D) and active community forum.
Many beginner guides still recommend it, so it has strong mindshare.

faq.q: Is Carbide Create free for LongMill owners?
faq.a: Carbide Create Core is free but is designed for Carbide 3D machines; exporting standard G-code for a LongMill or AltMill requires Carbide Create Pro ($120/year or $360 perpetual).

faq.q: Can Carbide Create send jobs to a LongMill directly?
faq.a: No. Carbide Motion only works with Carbide 3D machines, so you export G-code (Pro) and run it in gSender. CarvCAM designs, makes toolpaths and runs the LongMill/AltMill itself.

faq.q: Does Carbide Create work offline?
faq.a: Yes, it runs locally on Windows and Mac without internet.

faq.q: Does Carbide Create include feeds and speeds?
faq.a: Yes, it has a tool library with speeds and feeds focused on Carbide 3D tooling. CarvCAM's defaults come from Sienci's tables for your Sienci machine, router/spindle and bit.

faq.q: Which post-processor should I use for Carbide Create on a LongMill?
faq.a: Sienci recommends the grbl post-processor (Pro required for G-code output).

faq.q: Can I still get free G-code from older Carbide Create?
faq.a: Users report Carbide Create V6 still exports G-code, but it lacks newer features and is no longer the supported version.

sources.title: Carbide Create V7 blog (G-code in C2D)

competitors.name: Vectric VCarve Desktop / VCarve Pro (and Aspire)
competitors.type: CAD + CAM (no machine control; ships with the very basic VTransfer sender on Windows)
competitors.launched: unverified (current version V12.5, released May 2026 per reseller listing)

pricing.notes: Reseller list price (SainSmart, Woodcraft, OpenBuilds). Vectric's own page renders price client-side and was not captured. Major versions released within 12 months of purchase are free; minor updates free.
Sienci Labs (official reseller) lists $699 USD. Upgrade from Desktop by paying the difference.
Reseller list price; adds 3D relief modelling.
Trial cannot save toolpaths from your own designs (only sample projects), per users.

competitors.platforms: Windows only for VCarve/Aspire (Mac via Parallels, limited support). Vectric's separate 'Spark' product is new for macOS.
competitors.offline: Yes, desktop software; Sienci lists Vectric among options to design and generate G-code without internet
competitors.account_required: V&Co account / license code for activation and downloads (unverified whether ongoing internet check is needed; users report up to 3 installs)
competitors.runs_machine: No. Export G-code and run in gSender (Sienci's recommendation).
competitors.sienci_support: Strong: Sienci is an official Vectric reseller; Sienci's post-processor table lists 'grbl (mm)' and says newer Vectric versions may include a default 'LongMill' option; Sienci support documents a custom machine configuration for LongMill/AltMill. Sienci product pages say most customers use VCarve Pro or Carveco with gSender.
features: Full 2D drawing/editing, advanced text tools with single-line fonts, spell checker
Image tracing (vectorization); imports DXF, EPS, AI, SVG, SKP, PDF
Profiling with interactive tabs/bridges, lead-ins, ramps; pocketing; drilling; thread milling; auto-inlays
2.5D: V-carving, chamfer, fluting, prism, moulding, texture, PhotoVCarving, sketch carving
3D rough and finish of one imported 3rd-party model plus Vectric clipart
Toolpath preview/simulation with realistic material rendering (V12.5)
Toolpath tiling (both editions)
Pro only: unlimited job size, true-shape nesting, merged toolpaths, toolpath templates, gadgets, job setup sheets, keep-out zones, VCarve inlays, array copy toolpath
Aspire: 3D component modelling, sculpting, 90+ hours of tutorials

limits.text: VCarve Desktop work area is limited to 24 x 24 in; Pro is unlimited.
Desktop and Cut2D Desktop support jobs up to 24x24 in without tiling; larger jobs must be tiled into sections.
Vectric's comparison lists 'VCarve Inlays' as Pro-only (Desktop has auto-inlays).
VCarve Desktop can only import a single 3rd-party 3D model per job.
Windows only; Sienci notes Macs need Parallels and Vectric support may be limited.

pain_points.text: New LongMill 48x30 owner surprised Desktop is limited to 24x24 and asks for alternatives without the limit.
Desktop user: only drawback of the 24x24 limit so far is 'I can't surface my spoilboard.'
48-inch LongMill owner 'found out the hard [way] the 24 x 24 limitation'.
Sienci 2026 review: substantial upfront cost and Windows-only are the main knocks.
Trial can only generate G-code for Vectric's sample projects, so you can't fully test your own work before buying.

stronger: Industry-standard hobby/pro sign-making CAM with best-in-class V-carving and inlays.
Perpetual license; upgrade path Desktop to Pro to Aspire by paying the difference.
Enormous tutorial ecosystem (Vectric videos, Mark Lindsay CNC, Learn Your CNC) and many purchasable project files ship with Vectric instructions.
Far broader toolpath set: moulding, fluting, prism, texture, 3D roughing/finishing, nesting (Pro).
Sienci resells it and documents LongMill/AltMill machine configuration.
Regarded as intuitive by many users, including Sienci staff.

faq.q: Is VCarve Desktop enough for a LongMill 30x30 or 48x30?
faq.a: VCarve Desktop limits jobs to 24 x 24 in. Larger LongMill/AltMill beds require tiling or upgrading to VCarve Pro (about $699).

faq.q: How much does VCarve cost?
faq.a: VCarve Desktop lists at about $349 and VCarve Pro at $699 as one-time perpetual licenses; Aspire is about $1,995.

faq.q: Does VCarve run on Mac?
faq.a: VCarve and Aspire are Windows-only (Mac users use Parallels). CarvCAM runs on Windows and Linux today, with Mac in development.

faq.q: Can VCarve control my LongMill?
faq.a: No. You export G-code with the grbl (mm) post-processor and run it in gSender. CarvCAM includes machine control.

faq.q: Which post-processor should I use in VCarve for a LongMill?
faq.a: Sienci recommends Grbl (mm) or Grbl (inch) .gcode, not .tap, and suggests creating a LongMill/AltMill machine configuration.

faq.q: Is VCarve better than CarvCAM for 3D work?
faq.a: For 3D roughing/finishing, moulding, nesting and production features, VCarve/Aspire offer far more. CarvCAM focuses on signs, engraving, V-carving and cutouts with Sienci-tuned defaults.

Sienci Labs: Our relationship with Vectric

competitors.name: Autodesk Fusion (Fusion 360) for Personal Use
competitors.type: Full parametric 3D CAD + CAM + CAE (no machine control)

pricing.notes: Personal, non-commercial, home-based projects only; individuals generating < $1,000 USD/year; not for primary employment or commercial training.
30-day free trial; higher tiers (Fusion for Manufacturing/Design) cost more.

competitors.offline: Limited: cloud-based data management; an offline mode exists (per Sienci review) but requires periodic sign-in (duration unverified)
competitors.runs_machine: No. Post-process to G-code with the grbl post and run in gSender.
competitors.sienci_support: Sienci's post-processor table lists 'grbl' with required tweaks: Safe Retracts = Clearance Height (not G28), Output M6 = No, Output Tool Number = No. No official LongMill machine profile from Autodesk; users build their own.
features: Parametric and freeform 3D CAD, assemblies, sketches
2.5-axis and 3-axis milling CAM including adaptive clearing, turning, additive
Toolpath simulation in the Manufacture workspace
Large tool libraries; feeds/speeds are user-entered (no Sienci-specific defaults)
Huge learning resources and community

limits.text: Personal use removes rapid moves: all linking moves use high feed capped at the cut feedrate.
No automatic tool changes: operations using more than one tool must be posted as separate files.
Maximum of 10 active (editable) documents; others become read-only until swapped.
No probing, 3+2 or multi-axis milling; limited export formats; single-sheet drawings.
Non-commercial only and under $1,000 USD annual revenue.

pain_points.text: LongMill owner: 'Fusion 360 is free and crazy complicated'; months of YouTube to become competent; fears losing the hobby license.
Same user: frequent job failures on curvy Fusion/grbl files; fixes included disabling tool number and editing the post's decimals.
First test with a downloaded LongMill profile 'sent the router plunging into my wasteboard'; Z-zero mismatches between Fusion and gSender.
'Far too complicated to use for simple 2D and 2.5D carving.'
Personal-use users hit 'tool changer' post errors because multi-tool posting is blocked.
Fusion would not run on an office PC with integrated graphics.

stronger: True parametric 3D CAD: furniture, jigs, mechanical parts, assemblies; nothing CarvCAM-class can match it here.
Industrial-grade CAM (adaptive clearing, 3D finishing, aluminium-capable strategies).
Free for qualifying hobbyists.
Windows and Mac.
Massive tutorial base and community.
Skills transfer to professional work.

faq.q: Is Fusion 360 free for LongMill owners?
faq.a: Fusion for personal use is free for non-commercial, home-based projects by individuals earning under $1,000 USD/year, with CAM limitations.

faq.q: What are Fusion's personal-use CAM limits?
faq.a: No rapid moves (linking moves capped at cut feedrate), no multi-tool posting (one file per tool), 10 active documents, no probing or multi-axis.

faq.q: Which post-processor should I use for Fusion and a LongMill?
faq.a: Sienci recommends the grbl post with Safe Retracts set to Clearance Height (not G28), Output M6 = No, and Output Tool Number = No.

faq.q: Can Fusion run my LongMill directly?
faq.a: No. Export G-code and run it in gSender. CarvCAM includes machine control with guided zeroing and bit changes.

faq.q: Is Fusion overkill for signs and V-carving?
faq.a: Many LongMill users find Fusion powerful but complex for simple 2D/2.5D sign work. CarvCAM is focused on signs, text, engraving, V-carving and cutouts.

faq.q: Can I sell what I make with free Fusion?
faq.a: Personal use is limited to non-commercial projects; users generating over $1,000/yr must buy a subscription.

sources.title: Changes to Fusion 360 for personal use (Autodesk support)

competitors.name: Carveco Maker / Maker Plus
competitors.maker: Carveco Ltd (Warwickshire, England, UK); formed 2018 by former Delcam/Autodesk ArtCAM team
competitors.type: CAD + CAM, strong 3D relief (no machine control)
competitors.launched: Company formed mid-2018 after Autodesk discontinued ArtCAM (support ended Nov 1 2018); Carveco Maker product launch year unverified (~2019)

pricing.notes: Subscription only; 30-day free trial; auto-renews. (Raised from $15 on Sept 1 2025; Sienci's store page still shows $15.)
Adds 3D relief design, nesting, toolpath templates, tiling. Perpetual option listed at $1,200 on Carveco US store (unverified as current).

competitors.offline: Partially: needs internet to activate; then runs offline up to 21 days before it must re-check the license
competitors.account_required: Yes, email + license key activation against Carveco's license server
competitors.runs_machine: No. Export G-code and run in gSender.
competitors.sienci_support: Sienci is a Carveco reseller/affiliate; Sienci lists post-processor 'UGS grbl' (Sienci's Carveco store page says GRBL (in) or GRBL (mm)). Sienci product pages say most customers use VCarve Pro or Carveco.
features: 2D design and editing, Vector Doctor to fix imported vectors
2D/2.5D toolpaths, V-carving, inlays
3D model import (multiple models into one job), 3D machining
Maker Plus: Shape Editor, sculpting and texture tools for 3D reliefs, nesting, toolpath templates, batch calculation, tiling
AI Image-to-Relief and Text-to-Relief (subscription, credit-based)
No job size limit

limits.text: Maker is only available on subscription; stopping payment ends access.
Must reconnect to the license server at least every 21 days.
Tiling requires Maker Plus (per Sienci's 2026 review).

pain_points.text: Onefinity owner with a free year: hotkeys broken ('New Menu'), unclear docs, UI text hard to read; won't renew.
'Too many times I go to open the software and it errors saying it cannot connect.'
Activation failed with 'ExceededMachineAllowance' when moving to a new PC.
Beginner: 'still can't even make a simple sign without 52 problems arising' (vector errors, fillet/trim failing).
LongMill owner cancelling Carveco: issues with resizing, inlays, toolpaths that 'jump all over the project'.
Sienci 2026 review: 'I still don't find Carveco to be intuitive'; less tutorial content than Vectric.

stronger: Excellent 3D relief tools from 30 years of ArtCAM heritage; multiple 3D models per job.
Low monthly entry price, pause anytime.
No 24x24 job-size limit (unlike VCarve Desktop).
Vector Doctor auto-fixes messy imported vectors.
AI relief generation (credit-based).
Sienci resells it and many LongMill users run it.

faq.q: How much is Carveco Maker?
faq.a: $17.50/month or $180/year (subscription only). Maker Plus is $50/month or $540/year.

faq.q: Does Carveco Maker work offline?
faq.a: After activation it can run offline for up to 21 days before it must reconnect to verify the subscription. CarvCAM works fully offline.

faq.q: Which post-processor for Carveco and a LongMill?
faq.a: Sienci's table lists UGS grbl; Sienci's store page says GRBL (in) or GRBL (mm).

faq.q: Can Carveco control my LongMill?
faq.a: No, export G-code and run it in gSender. CarvCAM includes machine control.

faq.q: Is Carveco better for 3D reliefs?
faq.a: Yes, Carveco (especially Maker Plus) is strong for 3D relief work, which is outside CarvCAM's focus on 2D/2.5D signs, engraving, V-carve and cutouts.

faq.q: Is Carveco Windows only?
faq.a: Carveco lists Windows 64-bit system requirements.

sources.title: Getting Started With Carveco Maker (licensing/21 days)

competitors.name: Universal G-code Sender (UGS)
competitors.type: Sender (with a basic built-in designer for SVG/DXF/image import)

pricing.notes: Open source, GPLv3

competitors.platforms: Windows, Mac, Linux, Raspberry Pi (self-contained Java app)
competitors.runs_machine: Yes: GRBL, FluidNC, TinyG, g2core, Smoothieware (grblHAL works in GRBL mode; explicit grblHAL support unverified)
competitors.sienci_support: Listed by Sienci as a good alternative sender (difficulty 2/4); Sienci built gSender after feedback on older senders' flaws.
features: 3D G-code visualizer
Real-time overrides
G-code editor
Designer with SVG/DXF/PNG/JPG import and laser support
Gamepad and web pendant
Configurable G-code optimization

pain_points.text: LongMill users on the Sienci forum generally prefer gSender as 'way more user friendly' than UGS.

Long track record since 2012.

faq.q: Is UGS free?
faq.a: Yes, UGS is free and open source (GPLv3).

competitors.name: Kiri:Moto
competitors.type: Browser-based CAM (3D printing slicer, CNC, laser); no design, no machine control

pricing.notes: Open source (MIT per UGS wiki); donations welcome

competitors.sienci_support: Recommended by Sienci as a beginner-friendly 3D CAM (difficulty 2/4); Sienci's CAMLab is based on Kiri:Moto.
features: CNC operations: rough, outline, contour, pocket, trace, drill, lathe
STL-based 3D toolpaths
G-code preview

limits.text: CAM only from 3D models; you need separate design software and a sender.

stronger: Free 3D relief/tray CAM from STL in a browser.

sienci_recommendations.text: Sienci's 'Choosing Software' page recommends beginner Design+CAM options Vectr, Easel, Carbide Create, Inkscape, F-Engrave, Halftoner, Kiri:Moto and CAMLab; advanced options Carveco Maker, VCarve Desktop, Onshape, Fusion 360. It favours design-and-CAM-in-one tools.
For machine control Sienci recommends gSender as the go-to interface; UGS, CNCjs, OpenBuilds Control, Easel, VTransfer and bCNC listed as alternatives.
Sienci offers a Toolchain Wizard and a master software table of 80+ programs.
LongMill MK3 product page FAQ: 'most of our customers use Vectric VCarve Pro or Carveco for the CAM and gSender for the g-code sender.'

Sienci is an official reseller of Vectric (VCarve Desktop, VCarve Pro, Aspire) and a reseller/affiliate of Carveco; also lists LightBurn and MillMage. Sienci states the LongMill is fully compatible with free software.

Post-processor chart for LongMill/AltMill: Vectric grbl (mm); Carveco UGS grbl; Fusion grbl (with Clearance Height, no M6, no tool number); Easel none; Carbide Create grbl; Estlcam none; FreeCAD grbl (mm). Export in mm.
Sienci support article with Vectric machine configuration values (acceleration 1500 mm/s^2 AltMill, 750 mm/s^2 LongMill) and warning not to use .tap.
Sienci feeds & speeds tables (LongMill, Makita RT0701 dial settings, Sienci bits).
Sienci feeds & speeds Fundamentals page (reduced/regular speed tables in mm/min).
